From his childhood in Gary, Indiana, through the rise of The Jackson 5, and into the peak of his solo career during albums like Off the Wall, Thriller, Dangerous and HIStory, this documentary explores how Jackson’s voice evolved over time. By analysing Jackson’s vocal range, speaking patterns, and rare moments where his deeper register appeared, this video reveals what Michael Jackson really sounded like behind the carefully constructed King of Pop persona.

snippet.title: The Real Story Behind Michael Jackson & Paul McCartney’s Beatles Catalog Feud | the detail.
snippet.description:
For a brief moment in the early 1980s, Michael Jackson and Paul McCartney stood side by side at the top of the music industry. Their collaborations on 'The Girl Is Mine' and 'Say Say Say' united two of the most successful artists of their respective generations — the rising King of Pop and one of the legendary songwriters of The Beatles. What began as admiration and creative partnership soon became one of the most famous rivalries in music history.

From their early friendship and musical collaborations to the moment Jackson purchased the ATV Music Publishing catalog containing Lennon–McCartney songs, the story reveals how business decisions, music publishing rights, and commercial ambition transformed a creative partnership into a bitter dispute. What started as a shared passion for songwriting ultimately became a clash between two of the most powerful figures in popular music.

Using rare interviews, archival footage, and historical context, this film examines how Michael Jackson came to own the Beatles catalog, why Paul McCartney felt betrayed by the deal, and how the business of music publishing changed the relationship between two global icons. It also explores the wider implications of the acquisition — including how the Beatles’ songs were licensed, how the catalog later became part of Sony/ATV Music Publishing, and how McCartney eventually regained rights to portions of his music decades later.

Michael Jackson and Paul McCartney’s story is more than just a business dispute. It is a case study in the power of music publishing, the economics of the recording industry, and the complicated relationship between friendship and commerce at the highest level of pop stardom.
